narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Cloudier than yesterday; temperatures and winds little changed. Showery from the afternoon, with thunder possible, peaking this evening. 30°C / 86°F high, 20°C / 68°F low. Sky partly cloudy early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and overcast in the evening. Wind N early and SW at midday; gusts to 41 km/h (22 kt). UV index 9.4 (very high). Air quality 63 (moderate) at Dunga Beach, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 22°C / 72°F; low so far 20°C / 68°F; peak sustained 6 km/h; sky 4/8.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Monday, then partly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday. Rain loses support through Wednesday, from all four models Monday to one of four models Wednesday. Wednesday's call: dry, 28%, with one of four models wet; highs 30 to 33 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 57 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Thursday, showers and thunderstorms possible Friday, showers and thunderstorms likely Saturday, and rain and thunderstorms possible Sunday. Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Friday. GFS is the wetter solution from Thursday to Sunday; ECMWF, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Sunday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 80% of the time over 53 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability today: UKMO 3670 J/kg, ECMWF 2230 J/kg, ICON 1450 J/kg and GFS 640 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 41 km/h (22 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 29 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1015 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is filling over the next three days. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.3 and 1014.2 hPa, near-steady over three days (+0.3 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: +0.7 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 77% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 80% of the last 30 checks. On today's high GFS is the warmest model at 32.2 °C and ICON the coolest at 27.8 °C; the call's 30.0 °C sits between them. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind here.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
